guide.alien_fauna.title: Field Guide
guide.alien_fauna.cannonbolt.description: A gentle armoured alien that rolls up into a ball.
guide.alien_fauna.cannonbolt.habitat: Savanna and badlands, alone or in small groups. Now and then a baby is among them. A baby takes twenty minutes to grow up.
guide.alien_fauna.cannonbolt.behaviour: Wild ones wander slowly and now and then curl up and roll somewhere for fun, then stand dizzy for a moment. If hurt, one leans forward, curls up and rolls at whatever hurt it, then stands dizzy and takes extra damage. A ball cannot be hurt at all: a punch only sends it rolling and projectiles bounce off. A baby never fights.
guide.alien_fauna.cannonbolt.befriending: A melon slice calms an angry Cannonbolt, so no fight has to be finished. A few slices tame it. A tame one follows its owner, sits or stands with an empty-hand click, heals from melon slices and rolls at whatever attacks its owner. Two tame ones at full health, each fed a melon slice, breed, and their baby belongs to the same owner. Melon slices also make a tame baby grow up faster.
guide.alien_fauna.cannonbolt.drops: Nothing. A Cannonbolt never drops anything, and nothing in this mod needs one to be killed. The Field Guide itself is a book, a yellow dye and a melon slice.
item.alien_fauna.field_guide.tooltip: Use it on a creature to open its page.
guide.alien_fauna.intro: Strange creatures from beyond the stars have settled in the Overworld. This book is meant to help identify and chronicle them. Choose a creature on the right, or use the book on one to open its page.
message.alien_fauna.mounted: %s climbs on your back. Sneak and use a block to put it down.
guide.alien_fauna.gnoblar.description: Small, nosy and always underfoot. Secretly adorable.
guide.alien_fauna.gnoblar.habitat: Swamps, taigas and badlands, in chatty groups of two to four. Nobody knows how they got here, and they insist they came first. Their camps are easy to spot: a pot bubbling over a fire, two lopsided hide tents, a heap of precious scrap and a pumpkin on a pole of bones. Somebody is always home.
guide.alien_fauna.gnoblar.behaviour: Wild gnoblars are, frankly, a nuisance, and entirely harmless. They trot after visitors and squeak at them, and they carry off whatever is dropped, one item at a time, with great ceremony. It is not theft: the item is handed back for a gift, or dropped when they get bored. Every monster sends them fleeing with their arms in the air. At night they curl up on a hay bed with a carpet on top, and a jukebox sets them dancing. They never attack anything.
guide.alien_fauna.gnoblar.looks: No two are alike for long. Green, mossy, rusty, bark, pickle and sooty types wear their own sashes and wraps and have their own eyes, and some carry a proud wart on the nose, the cheek or the forehead. Plain green is the commonest. Sooty ones are the rarest.
guide.alien_fauna.gnoblar.befriending: Junk wins hearts: rotten flesh, bones, spider eyes, poisonous potatoes, dried kelp and brown mushrooms. A nose pickle (dried kelp and a brown mushroom, makes two) counts double. A brush wins a point of trust, and so does a water bottle used to wash off mud. Hit one and it remembers. Four points of trust make a friend, and no fighting is needed. A cake party warms a wild one up, but only a person can finish the job.
guide.alien_fauna.gnoblar.kindness: A friend follows, sits or wanders: click with an empty hand to change. Sneak and click to carry it piggyback, and sneak with an empty hand on a block to set it down. Dye colours its sash, a banner makes a hat (shears take it off) and food heals it. It sniffs scraps out of the soil, gets muddy doing it, and adores cake: one bite and the whole camp dances.
guide.alien_fauna.gnoblar.drops: Nothing. A gnoblar never drops anything but what it was carrying, and nothing in this mod needs one to be killed. Friends dig up flint, clay, sticks, bones and the odd gold nugget, and camp chests hold junk and the odd treasure.
